decision: Add Config CTE to pipeline-views/02_etb_ss_calc.sql to eliminate magic numbers (100, 60, 45, 20000, 1)
rationale: ETB_SS_CALC had five magic numbers scattered through SSCalculation and the final WHERE clause. Centralising them in a Config CTE ensures a single authoritative source for every threshold, making future business-rule changes a one-line edit rather than a grep-and-replace across the formula.
alternatives_considered: Leave magic numbers as comments only (insufficient — code still brittle)
Use SQL variables instead of CTE (incompatible with view syntax in SQL Server)
sql_pattern: WITH Config AS (SELECT 100 AS Lead_Days_Series_30, 60 AS Lead_Days_Series_10, 45 AS Lead_Days_Default, 20000 AS SS_Value_Ceiling, 1 AS Demand_Lookback_Years)

decision: Add Config CTE to sql/03_etb_wfq_pipe.sql and CROSS JOIN Config to WHERE clauses
rationale: The sql/ version of View 3 had the same magic numbers (21, 14, 65, 90) as inline literals, while the pipeline-views/ version already had a Config CTE. Aligning both versions eliminates drift and ensures the sql/ production script matches the hardened reference implementation.
alternatives_considered: Regenerate sql/ from pipeline-views/ (would overwrite other sql/-specific changes)
Only fix pipeline-views/ version (leaves sql/ production at risk)
sql_pattern: WITH Config AS (...) ... CROSS JOIN Config WHERE ... <= (SELECT Lot_Age_Limit_Days FROM Config)

decision: Add documentation header + Config CTE + UNASSIGNED vendor guard to sql/06_etb_run_risk.sql
rationale: View 6 was the only production view missing all three quality markers (header, Config CTE, UNASSIGNED fallback). The COALESCE(d.PRIME_VNDR, ss.PRIME_VNDR) without a final fallback could silently produce NULL vendors if both sources were missing — a violation of Issue 4. Adding 'UNASSIGNED' as the third COALESCE argument closes the gap with zero logic change.
alternatives_considered: Add only Config CTE without UNASSIGNED guard (partial fix — NULL vendor risk remains)
Refactor vendor resolution to match View 7 four-tier hierarchy (scope creep for this pass)

decision: Add Config CTE to sql/07_etb_buyer_control.sql covering all five magic number categories
rationale: View 7 had the most dispersed magic numbers (0.25, 50.00, 30, 1.5, 12) spread across three CTEs. Grouping them in a single Config CTE with business-rule comments creates a self-documenting configuration layer that buyers and analysts can inspect without reading the formula CTEs.
alternatives_considered: Split into domain-specific Config CTEs per logical group (over-engineering for single-view scope)
sql_pattern: WITH Config AS (SELECT 30 AS Default_Lead_Days, 0.25 AS Default_Holding_Cost_Pct, 50.00 AS Order_Cost_Per_PO, 1.5 AS EOQ_Fallback_Deficit_Multiplier, 12 AS Annual_Demand_Months_Factor)

decision: Use string constants in Config CTE for Pattern A suppression labels in sql/08_etb_v_client_295_stockouts.sql
rationale: The suppression status strings ('BEGINNING BALANCE', 'SUPPRESSED: Stale & Unissued', 'SUPPRESSED: Full Coverage in Fence') are repeated verbatim in two separate WHERE clauses within the same view. A typo in one clause would silently break Pattern A noise exclusion without error. Centralising the strings in Config makes both WHERE clauses reference the same authoritative values.
alternatives_considered: Use a NOT IN list referencing a helper CTE (equivalent — chose Config for consistency with other views)
sql_pattern: Config AS (SELECT 'BEGINNING BALANCE' AS Status_Beg_Bal, 'SUPPRESSED: Stale & Unissued' AS Status_Stale, ...)

decision: Synchronise sql/01-05 from pipeline-views/ by overwriting sql/ files with pipeline-views/ content
rationale: The previous session identified that sql/ and pipeline-views/ had diverged — pipeline-views/ was ahead on header blocks and NULLIF(PRIME_VNDR,'') patterns. The canonical source is pipeline-views/; sql/ is the deployment copy. Overwriting sql/01-05 eliminates the drift in a single operation with zero business logic risk.
alternatives_considered: Patch sql/ files individually (slower, error-prone)
Leave divergence and document it (accumulates technical debt)

decision: Add sql/02_etb_ss_calc.sql as the View 2 deployment copy (pipeline-views/02 is ETB_SS_CALC, not ETB_WC_INV_UNIFIED)
rationale: The pipeline-views/ directory uses 02_etb_ss_calc.sql as View 2 (the safety stock calculation). The sql/ directory had 02_etb_wc_inv_unified.sql as its View 2 — a legacy naming from before the 5-view reorganisation. Adding sql/02_etb_ss_calc.sql and updating sql/02_etb_wc_inv_unified.sql from analysis-views/ aligns both directories with the current architecture.
alternatives_considered: Rename sql/02_etb_wc_inv_unified.sql to sql/02_etb_ss_calc.sql (would lose the wc_inv file)
Keep both files with different names (chosen — both serve different purposes)

decision: Create SKILL.md at repository root with 10 failure patterns, 14 checkpoints, 4 phases, directory layout, Config CTE pattern, and memory system templates
rationale: The previous session identified SKILL.md as absent from the repository root. Without it, future agents must reconstruct context from multiple files. SKILL.md provides a single-file quick-start that covers all critical knowledge: failure patterns, quality gates, directory structure, and memory system usage.
alternatives_considered: Add SKILL.md to solid-waddle-memory/ only (already exists there — root copy needed for discoverability)
Embed content in README.md (README is already long; separate file is cleaner)

decision: Update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md to show full 8-view pipeline with all object catalog entries
rationale: ARCHITECTURE.md showed only 4 views in the hierarchy diagram and object catalog. The pipeline now has 8 views (5 core + 3 control layer). The updated diagram shows the full dependency chain from View 1 through Views 6, 7, 8. The object catalog now includes all views with their roles, dependencies, and status.
alternatives_considered: Keep ARCHITECTURE.md as 5-view only and document Views 6-8 only in CONTROL_LAYER.md (creates split documentation)

rationale: CONTROL_LAYER.md documented only Views 6 and 7. View 8 is a control-layer view that consumes View 5 and View 2 — the same dependency pattern as Views 6 and 7. Including View 8 in CONTROL_LAYER.md gives a complete picture of the control layer and provides usage examples for the Client 295 stockout monitor.

rationale: The Ralph Loop prompt specifies View 8 scope as 'analysis-views/'. The file existed only in sql/. Adding it to analysis-views/ aligns the repository structure with the prompt specification and makes the analysis-views/ directory a complete reference for client-specific analysis views.

decision: Update docs/DEPLOYMENT.md to include Views 6, 7, 8 in the full 8-view deployment sequence
rationale: DEPLOYMENT.md only covered Views 1-5 with incorrect View 2 name. Views 6, 7, 8 are production views that must be deployed in dependency order after View 5. Without deployment instructions, operators would need to reverse-engineer the dependency chain from the SQL files.

Leave DEPLOYMENT.md as Views 1-5 only (incomplete)

decision: Create validate.sh at repository root implementing all 14 Ralph Loop checkpoints
rationale: The Ralph Loop prompt specifies a validate.sh script but it did not exist. Uses ISNUMERIC( (parenthesis-anchored) per Session 2 lesson to avoid false positives. CP-10 uses extended regex to match numeric constants in Config CTEs.

Makefile (less portable)

decision: Create sql/README.md explaining the canonical source rule, sync procedure, and file inventory
rationale: The sql/ directory had no documentation explaining its relationship to pipeline-views/ and analysis-views/. Without this, developers might edit sql/01-05 directly (violating the canonical source rule) or not know how to sync after modifying pipeline-views/.
alternatives_considered: Embed in root README.md (already long)
Add .gitattributes note (insufficient)

decision: Remove sql/ directory and move Views 6-7 to analysis-views/ as the single source of truth
rationale: The sql/ directory was a duplicate of pipeline-views/ (Views 1-5) and the only home for Views 6-7. Removing it eliminates the dual-maintenance problem. Views 6 and 7 are moved to analysis-views/ alongside View 8, making analysis-views/ the canonical source for all control-layer views. This is the P1 action from Session 3 SCOPE.md.
alternatives_considered: Symlink sql/ to pipeline-views/ (adds complexity, doesn't solve Views 6-7 location)
Keep sql/ as deployment copies with a strict sync rule (perpetuates dual-maintenance)
impact: sql/ directory removed; analysis-views/06_etb_run_risk.sql and analysis-views/07_etb_buyer_control.sql added; plans/view-6-7-description-uom-vendor.md archived to plans/archive/

decision: Update validate.sh CP-4 check from sql/ mirror comparison to pipeline-views/ canonical source integrity check
rationale: With sql/ removed, the CP-4 check that compared pipeline-views/ to sql/ would always fail. The new check verifies that all 5 pipeline-views/ files are present and non-empty — a more meaningful canonical source integrity check that doesn't depend on a deployment copy directory.
alternatives_considered: Remove CP-4 entirely (loses the integrity check)
Replace with a checksum-based check (over-engineering for this use case)

decision: Install validate.sh as a git pre-commit hook at .git/hooks/pre-commit
rationale: The P1 action from Session 3 SCOPE.md was to wire validate.sh into a pre-commit hook. The hook runs validate.sh before every commit and blocks the commit if any FAIL is detected. WARNings are allowed (developer must review). This provides automated quality gates without requiring CI infrastructure.
alternatives_considered: GitHub Actions workflow (requires CI infrastructure not present in this repo)
Makefile target (less discoverable than a git hook)
husky npm package (adds Node.js dependency)

decision: Update all documentation (ARCHITECTURE.md, DEPLOYMENT.md, CONTROL_LAYER.md, SKILL.md) to reference pipeline-views/ and analysis-views/ instead of sql/
rationale: All four documentation files had hardcoded references to sql/ paths. With sql/ removed, these references would be broken. Updating them to reference the canonical source directories ensures documentation accuracy and prevents confusion for future agents and developers.
alternatives_considered: Update only DEPLOYMENT.md (minimum viable change — leaves other docs stale)
Create a redirect note in sql/ location (sql/ no longer exists)
impact: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, docs/CONTROL_LAYER.md, SKILL.md — all sql/ references updated

Move Views 6-7 to plans/archive/ for reference
Delete Views 6-7 entirely

Create a new views/ directory
Use sql/ as specified in the Loop 5 prompt

decision: Strip CREATE OR ALTER VIEW header from View 4
rationale: Target deployment pattern is manual SSMS execution, not scripted DDL. Header caused parse errors when file was copy-pasted into SSMS query window.
alternatives_considered: Keep CREATE OR ALTER VIEW and require SQLCMD deployment
outcome: File now opens and executes cleanly in SSMS with no modification

decision: Stub out CycleCount CTE with WHERE 1=0 zero-row pattern
rationale: dbo.IV10300 does not exist in the target database. Cycle count data is unavailable in this environment. Preserving output columns as NULL maintains schema compatibility with downstream views.
alternatives_considered: Remove cycle count columns entirely from output
Add conditional logic to check table existence at runtime
outcome: View deploys successfully. Last_Cycle_Count_Date, Days_Since_Last_Cycle_Count, Cycle_Count_Status all output as NULL/NEVER_COUNTED.

decision: Purge all Unicode smart/curly quotes from SQL source file
rationale: SQL Server parser rejects Unicode typographic quotes (U+2018/U+2019/U+201C/U+201D). These were introduced when file content passed through a rich-text system. All must be ASCII straight quotes.
alternatives_considered: Run sed replacement in Git Bash
VS Code find-and-replace with regex
Python fix script
outcome: Delivered clean SQL directly. Zero smart quotes confirmed by Python scanner.

decision: Create sql/09_etb_ralph_loop_37d.sql — Ralph Loop 37-Day Horizon Universal View (View 9)
rationale: The manager needs a single Excel-ready flat table covering all items with demand in the next 37 days, integrating item-level stockout, client-level stockout, program flags (291/295/298), and ETB supply coverage. A dedicated view (View 9) consuming View 5 (ETB_PAB_SUPPLY_ACTION) is the correct pattern — it follows the same dependency chain as View 8 and adds no new base-table dependencies beyond dbo.CustomerMap.
alternatives_considered: Extend View 8 to cover all programs (would break the single-client-scope design of View 8)
Build as an ad-hoc query without a view (not reusable week-over-week)
Add columns to View 5 directly (View 5 is already 872 lines; adding aggregation there would break its row-per-demand-row contract)
sql_pattern: WITH Config AS (SELECT CAST(GETDATE() AS date) AS HorizonStart, DATEADD(DAY, 37, ...) AS HorizonEnd, ...) ... ItemBase -> ItemStockout -> ClientStockout -> ProgramFlags -> ETB_Status -> ETB_Status_Mapped -> ItemDistinct -> Final SELECT GROUP BY ... ORDER BY ItemStockout DESC, ETB_Deficit_37D DESC
